public_rationale: The January 5 judicial order identifies numerous underlying copyright cases and resolves contested discovery objections involving OpenAI. That is sufficient to establish substantial ongoing litigation under the ordinary meaning of the claim. The conclusion does not depend on unverified counts of other lawsuits.
limitations: The evidence covers one consolidated litigation group, not OpenAI’s complete litigation portfolio.
Active litigation and adverse discovery rulings do not establish liability.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI is mired in a lot of litigation.

statement.excerpt: I warned that LLMs might plateau within a year or two, and they have, that OpenAI would be mired in a lot of litigation, and they are.
statement.document_title: The rapid rise and slow decline of Sam Altman

from_speaker: mired in a lot of litigation
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that OpenAI faces numerous active lawsuits involving substantial ongoing legal proceedings.
Mired does not imply that OpenAI has lost those cases or cannot conduct its business.
Use January 1–13, 2026 as the latest public-record reporting interval for this ongoing state. Litigation has no standard quarterly reporting period.
Assess the litigation limb independently of the neighboring plateau assertion.
criteria.support_condition: Dated records in the target period establish multiple substantial active lawsuits and ongoing contested proceedings involving OpenAI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Records establish that only isolated or insubstantial cases remain, or that the purported substantial proceedings have already ended.
